speaker: Doctor
text: Hello, I am Dr. Agent. I understand you are here for acute diarrhea; to help me determine the cause, how many loose stools have you passed in the last 24 hours, and have you experienced any fever or blood in your stool?

speaker: Patient
text: 58-year-old female. The patient has been treated for community-acquired pneumonia with levofloxacin on the medical floor. She reports developing watery diarrhea with at least 9 episodes within the last two days, accompanied by lower abdominal discomfort and cramping.

speaker: Doctor
text:
DIAGNOSIS READY: Clostridioides difficile infection (C. diff colitis).

Given your recent treatment with levofloxacin for pneumonia, the high frequency of watery stools, and abdominal cramping, this presentation is highly suspicious for antibiotic-associated colitis. I need to confirm if you have noticed any fever, recent hospital stays, or travel to finalize the assessment before ordering a stool assay.
